dimension_b_drift.title: slackMessageTs enforcement scope: pseudo says direction=outbound check; .md implements it inside !userId block
dimension_b_drift.evidence: docs/pseudocode/WF-60.pseudo:66 — Step 2 last bullet: 'transport == "slack" AND direction == "outbound" AND slackMessageTs (or alias) absent' — this check is NOT conditioned on userId absence; it is a standalone direction-scoped check. docs/pseudocode/WF-60.md:109 (Validate Inputs jsCode, decoded) — the slackMessageTs check is INSIDE the 'if (!userId)' block, meaning it is only enforced when userId is absent. For a slack+outbound payload that includes userId but omits slackMessageTs, the .md implementation would NOT throw, while the pseudo Step 2 says it SHOULD throw. This is a concrete pseudo↔md divergence on the enforcement scope of slackMessageTs. This is the OPEN parse-ambiguity question flagged in manifest cross-cutting note #3 and state.md followups #1. The reviewer cannot determine which is correct from sprint docs alone — §2.6 plain text says slackMessageTs is 'required on outbound (direction=outbound)' with no userId qualifier, which aligns with the pseudo (not with the .md implementation).
dimension_b_drift.recommended_action: Flag as question_for_human (see below). If §2.6 plain reading is canonical (slackMessageTs required on all slack+outbound regardless of userId presence), the Validate Inputs jsCode in n8n must be updated to move the slackMessageTs check outside the !userId block. If the intent is only to enforce it when userId is absent, then §2.6 and the pseudo Step 2 wording both need updating to reflect that qualifier.
